label: Figure 6
title: How 65 foundations and private grantmakers take requests, by kind of foundation (their own pages, read October 4–5, 2026)
caption: Each of the 65 foundation and private grantmaker records in this guide carries the foundation's own statement of how it takes requests. Twenty-three fund by invitation only and twenty-three only through calls they post; ten begin with a letter of inquiry; six accept an unsolicited request; for three the pages read state no policy. Ford's page reads "We do not accept any unsolicited grant proposals by mail, email or phone." [2259](#cite:2259) Simons takes applications only under its posted calls, and The Duke Endowment is among the six that accept a request [2119](#cite:2119) [2310](#cite:2310). Two of those six are corporate programmes that give software and services in kind [2446](#cite:2446) [2447](#cite:2447). The 65 are a sample chosen by the editor and not a ranking or a census, so the bars describe these records and nothing wider.
how_to_read: Each bar is one way of taking requests, and its height is the number of records that state it. The colours split a bar by the kind of foundation as the record gives it. Open the table to see which foundations stand behind a bar and follow the reference to the page where each says so. A foundation coded as invitation only may still read what it is sent, and one coded as taking letters of inquiry may fund few of them; the record's own note gives the wording.

explain.text: The foundation says it approaches the organisations it funds and does not take proposals it did not ask for [2259](#cite:2259).
The foundation takes applications only under a call it has posted, with that call's own deadline and eligibility rule [2119](#cite:2119).

A short first request; the foundation invites a full proposal from some of those who send one. Carnegie Corporation says "applicants may be invited via email to submit a full proposal" [2216](#cite:2216).

explain.on: Not stated on the pages read
explain.text: The pages read for the record give no policy on unsolicited requests. That is a gap in what was read, not a statement by the foundation.
The label on the funder record: independent, family, corporate, community, public-charity or medical-research-organization. One record carries no kind.

source: Counted by the builder from the unsolicited field of the 65 funder records that have one, grouped by the foundation_kind field. Each row lists its records and the references their notes cite. The statements are the foundations' own, as their pages stood on October 4 and 5, 2026. Nothing was converted; a count is a count of records.
